title: Tenant burst margin and eviction signalization for GPU memory budgeting
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Problem: We need a deterministic, tenant-aware memory margin system that lets tenants temporarily burst beyond their steady-state KV/activation reservation while preserving worst-case SLOs for other tenants. Current headroom policies are coarse: either generous static reserves (wastes GPU memory) or aggressive evictions that cause latency spikes and token-level errors. This ticket defines a design and rollout plan for: (1) soft burst lanes that allocate short-lived additional headroom per-tenant, (2) eviction signalization and graceful degradation hooks for runtime components (batcher, KV manager, weight-offloader), and (3) an emergency compaction path that prioritizes activation and KV compression before weight offload or request rejection.
background: We observed increased tail latency and elevated OOM rate during multi-tenant bursts (2025-01 incidents). Root cause analysis pointed to simultaneous KV growth + deep activations during long-context chats. Existing strategies (static watermarks + LRU eviction) either over-provision or produce noisy retries. Other eng tickets introduced predictive headroom sensors and KV slotting, but there's no tenant-level burst coordinator or standardized eviction signals consumed by batcher/optimizer subsystems.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a per-tenant burst_budget pool expressed in MB and a short TTL (e.g., 3s). The burst pool is funded from a small fraction of global slack and can be replenished adaptively.
proposed_solution_2: 2) Define eviction signal types: SOFT_TRIM (suggest compress/quantize KV segments), COMPACT_ACTIVATIONS (force activation compaction or trimming of unused frames), OFFLOAD_WEIGHTS (move non-hot weights to NVMe), and REJECT_SURFACE (final fallback). Each runtime component implements handlers for these signals with bounded latency.
proposed_solution_3: 3) Implement a token-aware decision function: for low-latency interactive requests, prefer KV compression and activation compaction before offload; for background batch inference, allow weight offload earlier. Decision function uses request metadata (priority tag, expected seq len, model family).
proposed_solution_4: 4) Create an emergency compaction path that runs incremental KV delta compression using lower-cost kernels and optionally drops cached prefixes >N tokens for inactive conversations, with explicit telemetry emitted so the console can show quality regressions.
experiments:
- Simulate multi-tenant bursts in staging using the tenant-burst-simulator harness (link: https://ci.redwood/gpu-sim/tenant-burst-sim).
- Run A/B: baseline vs burst-budget enabled on a 16-GPU cluster with mixed workloads (chat + embeddings) for 72-hour windows.
- Measure impact of SOFT_TRIM on token failure rates and response latencies for interactive flows.
- Run offline cost simulation to estimate median memory savings and additional NVMe IO from offload.
- PRs: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1287 (coordinator), /1299 (kv compressor), /1304 (batcher signal hooks)
metrics: Primary: 99th percentile latency for interactive calls, OOM rate per 100k requests, token-completion error rate. Secondary: NVMe write throughput, extra CPU used by compaction, percent time burst_budget in use. Dashboards: https://console.redwood/boards/gpu-memory/burst-budget
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime exposes per-tenant burst_budget metric and TTL.
- Batcher and KV manager implement and respond to defined signals within documented latencies (<50ms for SOFT_TRIM handlers).
- A/B test shows <=5% regression in median latency and >=30% reduction in OOMs during synthetic bursts.
- Console shows visibility into which tenant used burst budget and which signals fired.
- Runbook updated with clear escalation steps and rollback toggles.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gate behind runtime feature-flags. 2) Roll to internal infra team tenants (10 tenants) with low traffic for 48 hours. 3) Expand to canary set (50 tenants) and run A/B. 4) If metrics stable, enable for all non-enterprise tenants by default and gate enterprise behind contract opt-in. 5) Post-rollout: 7-day observation window and automated regression alerts.
risks:
- Incorrect signal ordering could cause premature weight offload and latency spikes.
- Burst budget misallocation could be starved by noisy neighbors.
- Compaction may degrade quality for long-context conversations if prefixes are trimmed without notice.
- NVMe offload increases IO bills and latency variability.
mitigations:
- Start with conservative burst pool size (1-2% of global slack) and increase only after experiments.
- Implement tenant-level fairness (max bursts per minute).
- Emit quality-change events to the Eval pipeline so regressions are tracked and can trigger automatic rollback.
- Add throttles on NVMe IO and fallback to REJECT_SURFACE only as last resort.
